By now this probably sounds terribly artificial. Is anyone actually going to do scheduled check-ins, delayed cohabitation, conversations about hypothetical disasters, imagination exercises, not to mention resisting the heat of the moment stuff, and continuing your own reparenting practices when a warm body is available to do some of the soothing?

Well, you caught me. It is painfully artificial.

That’s part of why. I’m trying to replace a missing community with instructions. If you actually have people around who know both of you, and other people to lean on when your partner is the wrong person, you need less of the instructions.

Maybe I am subtly trying to make you want to forget all this and just join a community. I couldn’t even say you’re wrong.

results.text:
## What doing it consciously looks like

Some of this I figured out by thinking. Most of it I learned by screwing up. Some of it I’m still testing.

- Have the big conversations before making love, especially the things that get harder to hear later: jealousy, attraction to other people, stress behavior, old patterns, how recent the healing is, what you want from each other in a hard moment, money. Give each other an actual situation. If X happened, what would you want, and what would you probably do? If you can only answer in generalities, I assume you probably don’t know yet.
- Don’t let sex, moving in, and deciding this is your life partner all become one decision. Housing can make separate living difficult, but once you share a home, practical necessity starts making some choices for you. Put a real check-in date on the calendar. And remember that a wonderful lover can still be a terrible co-parent, community member, or life partner. “I’m taking a chance on this person” is not the same as “this is the right person.” The second answer needs longer.
- Make deep friends together. Your old friends love you and hers love her, so of course they’re partial. That’s okay. Just don’t let them be the only people who know the relationship.
- Keep your inner practices. Being loved is not a reason to stop learning to love and regulate yourself.
- Pace the deep conversations too. Ten in one weekend can feel like a lot of depth before you’ve actually spent much ordinary time together. Some things you need to watch rather than ask about.
- If something in you says, Wait. Slow down. Something doesn’t fit. I need to ask this, listen to it before chemistry answers for you.
